diagrams.title: Electric heating and welding methods
diagrams.cap: Heating: resistance (direct or through an element), induction (eddy currents in metals), dielectric (HF field in insulators) and the arc furnace. Welding: resistance (spot, seam, butt, flash) uses I²Rt heat plus pressure; arc welding melts metal with an arc.
diagrams.qq: Which heating is used for wood and plastics?

diagrams.title: Traction speed–time curve
diagrams.cap: Area under the curve = distance. Average speed = distance/running time. Schedule speed = distance/(running + stop time) — less than average speed when there are stops (equal if no stops).
diagrams.qq: Which is larger: average or schedule speed?

diagrams.title: Illumination at a point (inverse square & cosine laws)
diagrams.cap: Directly below the lamp E = I/h². At an angle, use the slant distance d and multiply by cos θ (Lambert's cosine law).
diagrams.qq: 200 cd lamp, 2 m directly above. E?

formulas.name: Laws of illumination
f: Lambert′s cosine : E = I cos θd2
notes: Where: E = illuminance (lux), I = luminous intensity (cd), d = distance (m), θ = angle between the ray and the normal
Tip: Horizontal illumination under a lamp at height h: E = I cos³θ/h².

formulas.name: Lighting design

Tip: Depreciation factor = 1/MF.

formulas.name: Lamp efficacy

Tip: LED > CFL > fluorescent > incandescent (~15 lm/W).

notes: Where: tan δ = loss tangent

formulas.name: Induction heating
notes: Where: δ = penetration depth (m), ρ = resistivity (Ω·m), µ<sub>r</sub> = relative permeability, f = frequency (Hz)
Tip: For conducting materials; high frequency → surface hardening.

formulas.name: Traction speed
notes: Where: distance in km, times in h → km/h
Tip: Speed–time curve: acceleration, free running, coasting, braking.

formulas.name: Tractive effort
notes: Where: W = weight (tonne), α = acceleration (km/h/s), G = gradient (%), r = resistance (N/tonne)
Tip: Use effective (rotating) mass W<sub>e</sub> ≈ 1.1W in the acceleration term.

formulas.name: Batteries & electrolysis
notes: Where: m = mass deposited (g), Z = electrochemical equivalent (g/C), I in A, t in s
Tip: Wh efficiency < Ah efficiency.
Example: Charged 12 A × 10 h, discharged 10 A × 10.5 h: Ah efficiency = 105/120 = 87.5%. Copper Z = 0.000329 g/C, 5 A for 1 h: m ≈ 0.000329 × 18 000 ≈ 5.92 g.
TNPSC / ESE / APGENCO PYQ: TNPSC PG Q5

formulas.name: Power factor & energy
notes: Where: φ₁ = original, φ₂ = improved pf angle; kVAR = capacitor rating
Tip: Improving pf reduces current, losses and kVA demand charges.
Example: 50 kW from pf 0.7 to 0.95: kVAR = 50(1.020 − 0.329) ≈ 34.6 kVAR.
TNPSC / ESE / APGENCO PYQ: TNPSC 04/26 Q17

formulas.name: Electric & hybrid vehicles
f: Series hybrid: engine drives a generator, only the motor drives
parallel hybrid: engine and motor both drive the wheels
notes: Tip: EV batteries are secondary cells (Li-ion).

formulas.name: Trapezoidal speed–time curve & crest speed
f: crest speed V<sub>m</sub> = the highest speed of the run
notes: Where: D = run distance, T = running time, α = acceleration, β = braking retardation (one set of units); trapezoidal = accelerate, run free at V<sub>m</sub>, brake (no coasting)
Tip: Own example: D = 2 km, T = 180 s, α = 1 m/s², β = 1.5 m/s² → K = 0.833, V<sub>m</sub> = 11.75 m/s (42.3 km/h); with 30 s stop the schedule speed = 2000/210 = 9.52 m/s (34.3 km/h).

why.effect: E = I cos θ/d² (inverse-square and cosine laws).

mistakes.c: Inverse square: E = I/d², times cos θ for slant light.

mistakes.m: Induction heating needs the work to touch the coil
mistakes.c: The alternating field induces eddy currents in the work — no contact.

mistakes.m: Dielectric heating is used for metals
mistakes.c: Dielectric heating is for insulators (loss ∝ f tan δ); metals are heated by induction.
